title: Decode Nested Repeat String
statement: You are given an encoded string s built from lowercase letters, digits, and square brackets. The pattern k[inner] means the substring inner is expanded and then repeated k times, where k is a positive integer that may span several digits (for example 12[a] expands to twelve copies of 'a'). Brackets may nest arbitrarily, so 3[a2[bc]] expands to 'abcbcabcbcabcbc'. Return the fully decoded string. The input is guaranteed to be well-formed: every bracket is matched, every '[' is preceded by its repeat count, and s contains only lowercase letters, digits, and the characters '[' and ']'. A string with no brackets is returned unchanged.
hints: When you hit a ']', which part of the string needs to be repeated, and how do you recover the text that came before the matching '['?
Push the string built so far and the repeat count onto a stack at each '[', then reset your working string; pop and recombine at each ']'.

Accumulate multi-digit counts with num = num * 10 + int(ch). On '[' push (cur, num) and reset both. On ']' pop (prev, k) and set cur = prev + cur * k, so the inner block is repeated and re-attached to its outer context.
